result.summary: This PR reworks the scriptpubkeyman fuzz harness to remove redundant IsMine calls, cap the number of coins ConsumeCoins creates, move expensive operations (GetDescriptorString, GetNewDestination) out of the per-iteration hot loop, and fix a bug where the harness aborted execution instead of skipping when it could not update the wallet descriptor. It also restores and strengthens the IsMine/GetScriptPubKeys invariant assertion using the already-computed scripts set. The changes are limited to the fuzz test file and a small helper signature change in test/fuzz/util.{h,cpp}.
result.problem: The scriptpubkeyman fuzz target ran very slowly on the author's machine (reported under 40 exec/s, later measured with a real corpus at 200-300 exec/s by another contributor), limiting how much fuzzing coverage can be gathered per CPU-hour, and had a harness bug that aborted a run early rather than continuing to fuzz.

resolved_concerns: maflcko questioned removing an IsMine assertion covered implicitly by MarkUnusedAddresses; author clarified intent and restored a stronger assertion later.

pablomartin4btc noted the restored assertion only checked one random script instead of the full set and that the inverse-direction check was dropped; author agreed and restored the full assertion on 2026-08-19.

andrewtoth and ekzyis raised doubts about whether the reported speedup was real or corpus-dependent; ekzyis found the speedup only appears when running with a stale/no corpus, not with the real qa-assets corpus, but this was resolved as a misunderstanding rather than a criticism of the PR.

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: The PR is entirely about the fuzz harness for scriptpubkeyman: performance, coverage assertions, and a harness bug (early return), matching the Fuzzing label and the tests category's coverage of fuzzing harnesses.
categories.rationale: P3 because it is a worthwhile, reasonably deferrable improvement to fuzz harness throughput and correctness of its invariant checks. The author reports a large speedup on their machine (20 to ~150-385 exec/s under different sanitizer configs) and fixes a real early-return bug that previously stopped fuzzing on bad input instead of continuing; a contributor's independent measurement found the speedup is corpus-dependent, but the early-return fix and assertion strengthening stand on their own as harness-quality improvements.

uncertainties: Whether the measured speedup generalizes across environments is disputed in the discussion (andrewtoth, ekzyis got mixed results depending on corpus and sanitizer config); this affects how strong the performance claim is but not the presence of the bug fix.

Whether to classify this PR under wallet at all given it exclusively exercises wallet SPKM code, even though no wallet source is touched, is a judgment call; treated here as tests-only per the category's explicit carve-out.
result.card: This PR improves the scriptpubkeyman fuzz harness: it removes redundant IsMine calls, caps coin creation in ConsumeCoins, moves expensive operations (GetDescriptorString, GetNewDestination) out of the fuzz loop, and fixes a bug where the harness aborted execution instead of skipping bad input. The author reports a large exec/s speedup (20 to 150+ per iteration) though an independent contributor found the effect is corpus-dependent. A reviewer (pablomartin4btc) gave a specific concept ACK citing the early-return fix and hot-path cleanup as correct, and a follow-up concern about weakened assertion coverage was resolved when the author restored full IsMine/GetScriptPubKeys invariant checking on 2026-08-19. The PR touches only fuzz test code (src/test/fuzz/util.* and the scriptpubkeyman fuzz target), not wallet source, so it is a tests/fuzzing-infrastructure change rather than a wallet behavior change. It conflicts with open PR #35444 (descriptor SPKM mutex change) but has no stated blocking dependency.
